newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tanker owner says Tokio Marine, others cover repair.
newsitem.headline: Tanker owner says Tokio Marine, others cover repair.

text.p: Nippon Yusen KK, owner of the supertanker that hit a reef in Tokyo Bay and spilled oil on Wednesday, said on Friday that damage to the vessel will be covered by a group of insurance firms headed by Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd.
"Damage to the body of the ship is covered by several insurance companies, and Tokio Marine is the managing firm," a Nippon Yusen spokesman said.
Tokio Marine said it could not comment on contracts with its customers.
The 259,999 deadweight tonne ship scraped a reef in shallow waters in the bay, damaging three storage tanks.
The Nippon Yusen spokesman said it is not yet clear how much the repair work will cost.
The tanker is 75 percent owned by Nippon Yusen's Panamanian subsidiary and 25 percent by a Panamanian subsidiary of Ryoyu Tanker Co Ltd, which in turn is a subsidiary of Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
The crude oil cargo carried by the vessel was also fully insured, said a spokesman for Mitsubishi Oil, owner of the cargo, adding that no further information on the matter was immediately available.
The tanker, carrying 257,000 tonnes or about 300,000 kilolitres (kl) of crude at the time of the accident, spilled around 1,550 kl of crude into the bay.
